newsitem.title: USA: Wynton Marsalis wins Pulitzer Prize.
newsitem.headline: Wynton Marsalis wins Pulitzer Prize.

text.p: The Pulitzer Prize for music was awarded on Monday to Wynton Marsalis for his competition "Blood on the Fields."
"The winning composition has strong jazz elements, a first for this award in music since the inauguration of that category in 1943," said Seymour Topping, administrator of the Pulitzer Prizes.
The Pulitzer Prize for fiction was awarded to Steven Millhauser for his book "Martin Dressler: The Tale of an American Dreamer."
The winner of the Pulitzer Prize for poetry went to Lisel Mueller for "Alive Together: New and Selected Poems" published by Louisiana State University Press.
There was no award in drama for only the 14th time since 1917. Topping said none of the three plays entered fulfilled the criteria for the prize.

The Pulitzer Prize for general non-fiction went to "Ashes to Ashes: America's 100-Year Cigarette War, the Public Health, and the Unabashed Triumph of Philip Morris," by Richard Kluger, published by Alfred A. Knopf; the Pulitzer Prize for biography went to Frank McCourt for "Angela's Ashes: A Memoir," published by Scribner, and the Pulitzer Prize for history was given to Jack N. Rakove for "Original Meanings: Politics and Ideas in the Making of the Constitution," published by Alfred A. Knopf.
